newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Four U.N. aides helping with Algeria elections.
newsitem.headline: Four U.N. aides helping with Algeria elections.

text.p: The United Nations has only four consultants in strife-torn Algeria to help with Thursday's elections, not 100 as reported by some media, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Tuesday.
"There have been some misrepresentations or misreports of the U.N. presence in Algeria, saying we have 100 representatives there," he told reporters.

"In fact, in response to a request by the government of Algeria, we are providing technical assistants for the parliamentary elections there and these consist of four consultants who will brief observers, assist with their deployment throughout the country and facilitate their final debriefings. But the U.N. technical assistants will not judge the outcome of the elections," he added.

The voting for a 380-seat National Assembly will be the first parliamentary elections since the military-backed authorities in January 1992 scrapped a poll which the radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) was poised to win.

An estimated 60,000 people have since been killed in a wave of civil strife. Scores of villagers have been brutally massacred in the past few weeks while bombs blamed on Moslem guerrillas have killed at least 22 people and wounded more than 120 during the past three days.
